root_cause.text: The ath12k driver configures Wake-on-Wireless (WoW) offloads on all virtual interfaces (both primary and secondary links) in a multi-link connection, which triggers a firmware crash on WCN7850 hardware that only supports WoW offloads on the primary link.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that "WCN7850 firmware crashes due to WoW offloads enabled on both primary and secondary links," and the patch diff resolves this by adding checks (`arvif != &arvif->ahvif->deflink`) to skip WoW configuration functions (such as `ath12k_wow_set_wakeups`, `ath12k_wow_arp_ns_offload`, and `ath12k_gtk_rekey_offload`) for non-primary links.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict WoW cleanup to the default link virtual interface by skipping non-default links during iteration.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check 'arvif != &arvif->ahvif->deflink' inside the virtual interface iteration loop in ath12k_wow_cleanup.
intent_record.how: Ensures that ath12k_wow_vif_cleanup is only invoked for the default link interface, skipping any auxiliary or non-default link interfaces.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip non-default links when configuring Wake-on-Wireless wakeups to ensure settings are only applied to the primary interface link.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check within the virtual interface loop to skip entries that do not match the default link of their associated hardware interface.
intent_record.how: This restricts the Wake-on-Wireless wakeup configuration to only the primary default link, preventing incorrect or redundant configurations on non-default links.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict WoW NLO cleanup to the default virtual interface link to avoid incorrect operations on non-default links.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check inside the `list_for_each_entry` loop of `ath12k_wow_nlo_cleanup` to skip virtual interfaces (`arvif`) that are not the default link (`deflink`) of their corresponding hardware virtual interface (`ahvif`).
intent_record.how: This change restricts the Network List Offload (NLO) cleanup process to only run on the primary/default link of a virtual interface, preventing execution on non-default links.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict ARP/NS offload configuration to the default link of the hardware interface.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check to skip virtual interfaces that are not the default link of the hardware interface.
intent_record.how: Prevents the execution of ARP/NS offload configuration on non-default links during the interface iteration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict GTK rekey offload configuration to the default link of the virtual interface.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check inside the arvifs loop to skip iterations where the current arvif is not the default link (deflink).
intent_record.how: This change restricts the GTK rekey offload configuration to only execute for the primary/default link of the virtual interface, preventing redundant or incorrect offload setups on auxiliary links.

grouping_result.intent: Restrict WoW NLO cleanup to the default virtual interface link to avoid incorrect operations on non-default links.
Restrict ARP/NS offload configuration to the default link of the hardware interface.
Restrict GTK rekey offload configuration to the default link of the virtual interface.

consistency_review.core_intent: Restrict Wake-on-Wireless (WoW) configuration and cleanup operations to the default virtual interface link to prevent incorrect operations on non-default links.

relevance_review.reason: The group's changes directly address the vulnerability by restricting Wake-on-Wireless (WoW) configuration and cleanup to the default/primary virtual interface link, preventing the firmware crash caused by configuring WoW on secondary links.

The group's intent to restrict ARP/NS offload configuration to the default link directly addresses the root cause of configuring WoW offloads (such as ARP/NS) on secondary links, which causes firmware crashes.

GTK rekey offload is a type of WoW (Wake-on-Wireless) offload. Restricting its configuration to the default/primary link directly addresses the vulnerability where WoW offloads were incorrectly configured on secondary links, causing firmware crashes.
